sense: of a person or what they say: frank, straightforward

evidence: Cic. Rep. 3.26: quem apertum et simplicem volumus esse
Sen. Ep. 49.12: vēritātis simplex ōrātiō est
terms.comment: Frankly is simpliciter: simpliciter et līberē (Plin. Ep. 1.13.2, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: to stop beating about the bush, to come to the point
terms.grammar: phrase: ambāgēs, ambāgum f. pl., roundabout talk
evidence: Plaut. Cist. 747: ambāgēs, mulier, mitte atque hoc age
Hor. S. 2.5.9: missīs ambāgibus, without beating about the bush
terms.comment: Ambāgēs are roundabout ways, of a road or of talk. Terence’s answer to a rigmarole: mitte: ad rem redī, drop it, get to the point (Heaut. 319).

phrases.latin: sed quaesō, ambāgēs, mulier, mitte atque hoc age. ēloquere, unde haec sunt tibi, cito, crepundia
phrases.english: but please, woman, stop beating about the bush and attend to this. Tell me, quickly: where did you get these trinkets?

phrases.latin: Quās, malum, ambāgēs mihi narrāre occipit? — Syre, vērum hic dīcit; mitte: ad rem redī.
phrases.english: What’s this rigmarole he’s started telling me? — Syrus, he’s right: drop it and get to the point.
the language of truth is simple
